title: Wire pipeline_error_handler into the orchestrator — the execution log exists but no pipeline run has ever written to it
description: pipeline_error_handler.Notebook is a complete 521-line implementation (error categorization against transient/permanent pattern lists, gold_pipeline_execution_log schema + ensure_log_table_exists, log_activity_start/success/failure, get_execution_summary, failure reporting, get_retry_effectiveness) that nothing calls. It is not an activity in orchestrator_pipeline_bronze_to_gold, no notebook %run's it, and gold_pipeline_execution_log is referenced by no other artifact in fabric/ — so the table is never populated by an orchestrated run and every reporting function queries an empty table. All 8 pipeline activities depend on their predecessors with dependencyConditions ['Succeeded'] only; there is no Failed branch anywhere in the pipeline, so no failure path exists to log from. Retry policies ARE configured and do work (retry 3/3/2/3/2/2/2/1; empirically confirmed when data_quality_checks with retry=1 produced two attempts that failed identically), so what is missing is observability of failures, not resilience against them. Closing this is a precondition for task-037, whose criteria assert that a failure is written to the execution log and that a notification fires.
acceptanceCriteria: The failure-propagation topology is DECIDED and recorded before implementation. SETTLED BY DEC-004 (decided 2026-07-23): Option A — pipeline-level on-failure activities using dependencyConditions ['Failed', 'Skipped'], fanned in on the terminal activity plus a trailing Fail activity: 2 activities total, NOT 8. This criterion originally warned that 'Fabric ANDs multiple dependsOn entries on one activity, so guarding N activities is not simply one handler with N dependencies'. The AND premise is correct and Fabric-doc-confirmed, but the inference was wrong for THIS pipeline: it is a single convergent DAG in which all 8 activities are ancestors of data_quality_checks, and 'Skipped' propagates transitively — so the documented 'Generic error handling' fan-in covers all 8 with one handler. Implementation must read per-activity outcomes via POST queryactivityruns, NOT @activity('X').Error, because skipped activities carry no error field. Revisit only if the DAG stops being singly-terminal: a tail fork would silently un-cover the new branch. (Closes FR-015.)

A failure in at least one Copy or RefreshDataflow activity (i.e. a non-notebook activity) results in a row in gold_pipeline_execution_log. This is the coverage case option B cannot satisfy and is the reason the topology decision matters — do not let the criterion collapse to notebook-only logging without an explicit, recorded scope reduction.

A successful orchestrated run also populates the log (log_activity_start / log_activity_success), so get_retry_effectiveness and get_execution_summary have both outcomes to compare rather than only failures.

error_category is populated from categorize_error() on logged failures, and at least one real failure is confirmed to land in a sensible category — the transient/permanent pattern lists have never been exercised against a live Fabric error string.

The notification sink is configured or explicitly deferred with a reason. All three RefreshDataflow activities currently carry "NoNotification" and the pipeline JSON contains no email/Teams/webhook configuration of any kind, so task-037's notification criterion has nothing to exercise today. Deferring is acceptable; leaving it undecided is not.

[Erik/Fabric] Deployed and demonstrated end-to-end: induce a failure, confirm the log row appears with a usable error message, timestamp, retry_attempt and pipeline_run_id, then confirm a clean run logs its successes.
task-037's status is reconciled once this lands — it is currently Pending with criteria that cannot pass, and should either be unblocked or have its dependency on this task recorded.

That criterion required the pipeline_error_handler decision be RECORDED (it was: 'spun into its own task, not wired here, not silently deferred'), but the promised task was never created. task-026 is Finished on its own terms; this is the follow-through.

VERIFIED UNREFERENCED (with a positive control, per rules/agents.md § Negative Findings): grep for 'pipeline_error_handler' across fabric/ returns only its own .platform file; grep for 'gold_pipeline_execution_log' returns only the handler notebook plus two documents (error_recovery_playbook.md, error_handling_strategy.md). Control probe for 'silver_procurement' over the same tree returned 3 files, so the search works and the absence is real rather than a failed probe.

PIPELINE STATE AT CREATION: 8 activities — bronzecopy_EUSupplyShares, bronzecopy_GlobalSupplyShares (Copy); bronze_WGI, bronze_procurement, bronze_EPI (RefreshDataflow); bronze-to-silver data cleaning, silver-to-gold, data_quality_checks (TridentNotebook). Every dependsOn uses dependencyConditions ['Succeeded']. Retry policies: 3, 3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 1.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN: retry logic works and is proven — data_quality_checks with retry=1 produced exactly 2 attempts on the 2026-07-22 18:41 and 20:16 runs, both failing identically. task-011 delivered real resilience. The gap is purely that failures leave no durable trace, so there is no way to answer 'how often does this pipeline fail, on what, and do retries rescue it'.

BLOCKS task-037 ('Test pipeline error handling and retry logic with simulated failures'): its criterion 2 asserts the failure is written to the execution/error log table, and criterion 3 asserts a notification fires. Neither can pass today — nothing writes the table and notifications are off. task-037 is Pending and looks routable, which is misleading; record the dependency when this task is picked up.

RELATED to task-040 (DQ gate verdict not persisted). Both are the same class of defect — the pipeline's observability artifacts exist but are not connected to the runs they describe — but they are separate surfaces: 040 covers gold_quality_history and the DQ gate's outcome, this covers gold_pipeline_execution_log and activity-level failures. Do not merge them; a single run can pass every DQ check and still fail at a Copy activity.

DESIGN CONTEXT from task-026's deferral rationale: this needs a failure-propagation topology decision AND a notification sink Erik configures, which is why it was kept out of 026 rather than bundled — wiring it there would have conflated the DQ gate with general pipeline error handling.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: this task does not change retry counts, does not alter the DQ gate, and does not add new error categories. It connects an existing, complete implementation to the pipeline that should be feeding it.

GATED ON DEC-004 (2026-07-23): criterion 1's failure-propagation topology was filed as a decision record (.claude/support/decisions/decision-004-pipeline-failure-propagation-topology.md) rather than decided inline, per criterion 1's own instruction and rules/decisions.md. research-agent is populating its four open questions: (1) does Fabric AND multiple dependsOn entries on one activity — decides whether Option A costs 1 handler or 8; (2) can a parent pipeline recover WHICH child activity failed — decides whether Option C is usable; (3) what failure context is reachable from @activity()/@pipeline() system variables — log_activity_failure needs activity name, error message, pipeline_run_id and retry attempt; (4) what notification sink is actually available (criterion 5). Do not start implementation until Erik ticks a box.

DEC-004 RESEARCHED 2026-07-23 — and it OVERTURNS this task's criterion 1. The AND premise is correct (now Fabric-doc-confirmed on the Outlook activity page), but the cost inference is wrong for THIS pipeline: the 8 activities form a single convergent DAG whose only terminal node is data_quality_checks, and Skipped propagates transitively, so the documented 'Generic error handling' fan-in — one handler on the last activity via BOTH Failed and Skipped — guards all 8. Option A costs 2 activities (handler + Fail), not 8. Criterion 1's '1 vs 8' cost framing should be corrected via /iterate when the decision lands. Tracked as FR-015.

TRAP found by research, not previously recorded anywhere: attaching an on-failure branch to the terminal activity produces the documented Try-Catch shape, which makes the overall pipeline run report SUCCESS when the handler succeeds. That would silently undo task-026's DQ gate — every failing run would go green. A trailing native Fail activity on the handler's Succeeded path is REQUIRED, not optional. No Fail/Invoke/Web/Outlook activity exists in fabric/ today (verified with a positive control).

TWO PREREQUISITES this task's cost model omitted, applying to Options A and C alike: (1) pipeline_error_handler has NO parameter cell, and parameter cells are a Fabric-UI toggle that cannot be hand-authored in notebook-content.py — Erik must toggle one before any parameter reaches the handler, which makes this task owner:both on the Fabric side regardless of option. (2) The handler's logging API is two-phase (log_activity_start returns a UUID that log_activity_failure UPDATEs); a pipeline-level failure branch has no start call to pair with, so a one-shot log_activity_outcome(...) must be added. Option B is the only option whose API fits as written.

CRITERION 5 CAN BE ANSWERED, NOT DEFERRED: four real sinks found. Cheapest credible is scheduled-run Failure notifications (Home > Schedule > Failure notifications) — zero pipeline JSON, zero CI/CD exposure — whose one documented gap is 'notifications aren't sent for on-demand runs', exactly what task-037's induced-failure test would be. Pair with an Activator rule on pipeline job events to close it. The Outlook/Teams activity is the only sink that can show the actual error text but is documented 'inactive when using CI/CD' — a re-binding chore on every deploy.

EXPERIMENT REQUIRED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION (~30 min, throwaway artifacts): does queryactivityruns return rows for a run that is STILL IN PROGRESS? The handler executes inside the run it would query and the docs do not address it. Scratch pipeline: Wait(2s) -> a deliberately-failing activity -> a scratch notebook on ["Failed","Skipped"] that POSTs queryactivityruns with @pipeline().RunId and prints the raw response. Rows present -> recommended shape confirmed. Empty/404 -> fall back to Option A's 8-handler form with literal names and @activity('X').Error.Message. 401/403 -> the notebookutils getToken('pbi') scope caveat bit; needs MSAL or a workspace-identity connection.

TRY-CATCH TRAP CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY 2026-07-26 (was research-only until now). Scratch pipeline scratch_qar_test (Wait1 -> Fail1 via Succeeded; Fail1 -> Notebook1 via Failed) run 3bda2a8f-7f13-45a1-b9c7-1347ba4092ae: Fail1 reported Failed, Notebook1 reported Succeeded, and the PIPELINE STATUS REPORTED 'Succeeded'. This is the exact failure mode DEC-004's research warned about — a handler on a failure branch that succeeds turns the whole run green. Confirms the trailing native Fail activity on the handler's Succeeded path is REQUIRED, not optional; without it task-026's DQ gate is silently undone and every failing run looks healthy. Prior evidence was Microsoft docs only; this is a live run in this workspace.

STEP 1 PROGRESS 2026-07-26: scratch artifacts built and wiring verified working — scratch_qar_test pipeline (34ad330f-7441-4ab0-9af2-25a0efbf4479) + scratch_qar notebook (2b1aee35-ed18-4989-8d20-53cc56078740). Took three runs to get the topology right; the first two attached Notebook1's dependency to Wait1 rather than Fail1 (an unmet dependency makes the activity vanish from the run output entirely rather than error — 'Showing 1-2 items' was the only symptom). Usable historical run ids in this pipeline: 3bda2a8f-7f13-45a1-b9c7-1347ba4092ae (3 activities), 6189b2d8-e748-4632-96bb-bba812c947c4, 90b80126-e648-4787-a6b0-e27f38223308.

STEP-1 EXPERIMENT RUN 1 (2026-07-26, pipeline run 3bda2a8f-7f13-45a1-b9c7-1347ba4092ae). TWO OF THREE BRANCH QUESTIONS SETTLED, both favourably. (a) PARAMETER INJECTION WORKS END TO END: the Item-snapshots view shows the Parameters badge on cell 1, Fabric's auto-generated override cell directly beneath it setting p_run_id='3bda2a8f-...', and an Input-parameter grid confirming p_run_id | string | 3bda2a8f-.... The parameter-cell mechanic is proven for the real handler. (b) TOKEN SCOPE IS NOT AN ISSUE: notebookutils.credentials.getToken('pbi') produced a token the API accepted — the response was 404 EntityNotFound, not 401/403, so the MSAL / workspace-identity fallback branch is CLOSED. (c) The in-progress question is still OPEN because the probe URL was wrong.

SCAFFOLD URL DEFECT (mine, not Erik's) — the runbook's queryactivityruns URL carried an extra pipeline-id segment: .../datapipelines/{pipelineId}/pipelineruns/{runId}/queryactivityruns. Per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-factory/pipeline-rest-api-capabilities the correct shape has NO item id: POST /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/datapipelines/pipelineruns/{jobId}/queryactivityruns. The body also cannot be {} — documented payload is {filters:[], orderBy:[{orderBy:'ActivityRunStart',order:'DESC'}], lastUpdatedAfter, lastUpdatedBefore}. Both fixed in RUNBOOK-task-041.md. RESPONSE SHAPE (documented sample) is a BARE JSON ARRAY, not {value:[...]}, so an empty result reads as []. Fields returned: pipelineName, pipelineRunId, activityName, activityType, activityRunId, status, activityRunStart, activityRunEnd, durationInMs, input, output, error{errorCode,message,failureType,target,details}, retryAttempt, recoveryStatus — every argument log_activity_outcome() needs, including retryAttempt which is what makes get_retry_effectiveness() meaningful. OPEN CAVEAT: docs say the job id 'is the same ID created and used in the Job Scheduler Public APIs' while the run-detail pane labels our value 'Run group ID'; if the doc-correct URL still 404s, that mismatch is the next suspect.

STEP-1 EXPERIMENT RUN 2 (2026-07-27, pipeline run f929fee8-0440-4867-9da9-9264c2ad6f47). Doc-corrected URL returns HTTP 200 — endpoint shape CONFIRMED as POST /v1/workspaces/{ws}/datapipelines/pipelineruns/{runId}/queryactivityruns. RESULT WAS EMPTY: {"value": [], "continuationToken": null}. RESPONSE-SHAPE CORRECTION: the live API returns an OBJECT with `value` + `continuationToken`, NOT the bare JSON array shown in the Microsoft Learn sample — code must read r.json()['value'], not r.json(). NOT YET CONCLUSIVE — see next note.

AMBIGUITY BLOCKING THE DEC-004 SHAPE CHOICE (2026-07-27): the empty 200 has TWO candidate explanations and they lead to opposite implementations. (a) queryactivityruns genuinely returns no rows for a still-in-progress run — the handler executes inside the run it queries, so the 2-activity fan-in is impossible and Option A's 8-handler per-activity @activity('X').Error form is required. (b) The run id is wrong: docs state the job id 'is the same ID created and used in the Job Scheduler Public APIs', while the Fabric run-detail pane labels the value we passed 'Run group ID'. A valid request with a non-matching id would also return 200 + empty. Evidence that (a) is not yet established: at the moment the handler ran, Wait1 had already Succeeded and Fail1 had already Failed, so completed activities DID exist in that run. DISAMBIGUATION (cheap, ~2 min, no pipeline run needed): execute the same probe interactively with p_run_id hardcoded to a COMPLETED historical run (e.g. 3bda2a8f-7f13-45a1-b9c7-1347ba4092ae). Rows -> explanation (a), in-progress is the blocker. Still empty -> explanation (b), the id semantics are wrong and the 2-activity shape may still be viable once the job-instance id is resolved. DO NOT pick the 8-handler fallback before this runs.

RUN-ID SEMANTICS RESOLVED 2026-07-27 — @pipeline().RunId IS the job-instance id. GET /v1/workspaces/{ws}/items/{pipelineId}/jobs/instances returned 5 instances whose `id` values (f929fee8-0440-4867-9da9-9264c2ad6f47, 8a6d1260-f413-4d81-ac99-7d7324b08579, 3bda2a8f-7f13-45a1-b9c7-1347ba4092ae, 6189b2d8-e748-4632-96bb-bba812c947c4, 90b80126-e648-4787-a6b0-e27f38223308) are IDENTICAL to the 'Pipeline run ID' / 'Run group ID' values shown in the run-detail pane and injected by @pipeline().RunId. The docs' warning that the queryactivityruns job id 'might be different from the Get item job instance API' does NOT apply here. Both earlier hypotheses are therefore eliminated: it is neither an in-progress limitation (a COMPLETED run returns empty too) nor an id mismatch.

OPEN 2026-07-27: queryactivityruns returns HTTP 200 with {"value": [], "continuationToken": null} for a COMPLETED run whose failureReason is populated in the jobs/instances listing. Remaining suspects, in order: (1) the request body omitted lastUpdatedAfter/lastUpdatedBefore — these were dropped from the probe to reduce paste-mangling risk, but Microsoft's documented sample includes both, and a narrow server-side default window would produce exactly this empty result; (2) token scope — notebookutils.credentials.getToken('pbi') yields a Power BI-scoped token that authenticates (no 401/403) but may return no activity-run data, needing an api.fabric.microsoft.com scope; (3) capacity/SKU limitation on a trial capacity. NOTE the jobs/instances endpoint DOES return rich data with the same token, including failureReason.errorCode/message ('TEST001', 'Operation on target Fail1 failed: deliberate test failure') — which is itself a candidate fallback data source for the handler if queryactivityruns stays empty, though it is pipeline-level rather than per-activity.

*** STEP-1 EXPERIMENT CONCLUDED 2026-07-27 — queryactivityruns DOES return rows for a STILL-IN-PROGRESS run. DEC-004 Option A's 2-activity fan-in is CONFIRMED; the 8-handler per-activity fallback is NOT needed. Evidence: pipeline run 7c2781b8-6ad2-4bd6-bf0d-ff8acccf6991, handler notebook executing as Notebook1 INSIDE that run, printed: status 200, activity count 3, 'Notebook1 | InProgress |', 'Fail1 | Failed | deliberate test failure', 'Wait1 | Succeeded |'. All three activities visible from inside the live run, with the failing activity's error message populated.

ROOT CAUSE of the three earlier empty results was the REQUEST BODY, not the API: lastUpdatedAfter / lastUpdatedBefore are MANDATORY in practice. They were dropped from the probe to reduce paste-mangling risk; without them the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an empty value array for every run, completed or in-progress, which mimics both a wrong-id and an in-progress limitation. Microsoft's documented sample includes both fields. Use a wide window (e.g. 2020-01-01 .. 2030-01-01) in the handler.

HANDLER IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS established by the experiment: (1) THE HANDLER SEES ITSELF — its own activity appears in the results with status 'InProgress'. It must skip its own activity name (or skip status=='InProgress') or it will log a phantom row for itself on every run. (2) The `error` object is ALWAYS PRESENT, even on success, as errorCode/message/failureType/target/details with empty strings — so branch on `status`, never on error-presence; `if a['error']` is truthy for every activity. (3) Response is an OBJECT: read r.json()['value'], not r.json(). (4) Field mapping confirmed live: activityName, status, error.message, pipelineRunId, retryAttempt (null when no retry), activityRunStart/activityRunEnd/durationInMs, activityType. (5) Successful activities carry an empty error.message, so error_message should be stored NULL rather than ''.

CRITERION 5 DECIDED 2026-07-27 — NOTIFICATION SINK DEFERRED, with reason (criterion 5 permits deferral, not silence). Erik's call. Reason: the original plan (notifyOption='MailOnFailure' on 'the 3 RefreshDataflow activities') was invalidated by the EPI/WGI repoint — only bronze_procurement is still a RefreshDataflow, so that sink would now cover 1 of 8 activities and read as coverage while a Copy or notebook failure sends nothing. The two remaining options each carry a disqualifying flaw at this stage: schedule-attached Failure notifications do not fire for on-demand runs (which IS task-037's induced-failure test), and the Outlook/Teams activity is documented inactive under CI/CD, requiring a manual re-bind after every git Update — directly against the deployment story this project demonstrates. REVISIT when task-010 (Configure Pipeline Scheduling, currently On Hold) lands, since a schedule is what makes the zero-JSON sink meaningful. Until then the pipeline's failure signal is gold_pipeline_execution_log plus the run reporting Failed via fail_orchestrator_run.

STEP 3 AUTHORED 2026-07-27 (inline, no agent). (a) pipeline_error_handler.Notebook: appended the harvest cell — fetch_activity_runs() POSTs queryactivityruns with the mandatory lastUpdatedAfter/Before window; harvest_pipeline_run() maps Succeeded->SUCCESS / Failed->FAILED and calls the existing one-shot log_activity_outcome() per activity, logging successes too (criterion 3). Skips its own activity by name (it appears as InProgress), skips non-terminal statuses, coerces null retryAttempt to 0 and empty error.message to NULL, and truncates Fabric's 7-digit fractional seconds to the 6 datetime.fromisoformat accepts. RAISES RuntimeError on an empty activity list rather than logging nothing — the branch only fires when something failed, so empty means the query is broken, which is precisely the silent no-op this task exists to remove. (b) pipeline-content.json: +pipeline_error_handler (TridentNotebook, notebookId = the .platform logicalId d4e5f6a7-..., dependsOn data_quality_checks via ['Failed','Skipped'], p_run_id=@pipeline().RunId, retry 0 deliberately so a partial write is never duplicated by a retry) and +fail_orchestrator_run (native Fail on the handler's Succeeded path). Patch script guards on the DAG still being singly-terminal before applying. VERIFIED LOCALLY: 12-assertion harness against the real observed payload (self-skip, Skipped exclusion, null-retry coercion, empty-message->NULL, duration 292063ms round-trip, fail-loud on empty) all pass; notebook parses as valid Python; pytest 94/94.

DEC-004 TOPOLOGY AMENDED 2026-07-27 (Erik approved). The as-built failure-only handler could not satisfy criterion 3. PROOF: orchestrator run b5d799b1-3643-45d9-9a63-bcae0cc8199a — the first run after deploying the original Step 3 — completed 8/8 Succeeded and wrote ZERO execution-log rows, because pipeline_error_handler hung off ['Failed','Skipped'] of data_quality_checks and therefore never fired on a clean run. Criterion 3 requires that a SUCCESSFUL orchestrated run also populates the log so get_execution_summary/get_retry_effectiveness have both outcomes to compare. AMENDMENT: handler now depends on data_quality_checks via ['Succeeded','Failed','Skipped'] (runs on every outcome) and the notebook RE-RAISES after writing all rows if any activity logged FAILED. That raise fails the handler activity, which keeps a failing run red — the same Try-Catch defence the trailing Fail activity provided. fail_orchestrator_run was REMOVED: under the new shape it sits on the handler's Succeeded path, so a clean run would reach it and be wrongly marked Failed. Net: 1 activity instead of 2, and criteria 2 and 3 are served together. DEC-004's substance is unchanged (single handler on the terminal activity, queryactivityruns, explicit guard against green-on-failure); only the guard MECHANISM changed, from a trailing Fail activity to an in-notebook raise. DEC-004's record should be updated via /research + checkbox to reflect this.

DEPLOY VERIFIED 2026-07-27: the git Update landed cleanly — all activities present in the live pipeline, notebookId resolved from the .platform logicalId as expected, and run b5d799b1 executed 8/8 with all four parameters passed. NOTE for the runbook and for task-036/037: the prediction that a workspace Update from git would unbind the dataflows did NOT hold this time — bronze_procurement bound fine and ran clean. [[fabric-dataflow-connection-bindings]] describes a real 2026-07-22 event but it is not deterministic, so an induced failure cannot rely on it; use a deliberate Copy-source break instead.

CRITERION 2 + 6 (failure half) DEMONSTRATED LIVE 2026-07-27, orchestrator run 742ff1ff-42d8-4fb6-9845-8c7a183c060d. Induced a genuine NON-NOTEBOOK failure by setting bronzecopy_GlobalSupplyShares' Relative URL to 'does-not-exist.csv' (the field is normally empty; the whole path lives in the connection's base URL, so reverting = clearing it). Result: the Copy failed 4 times (retry 3, retryIntervalInSeconds 300 — ~19 min end to end), bronze-to-silver/silver-to-gold/data_quality_checks went Skipped, the handler fired on that Skipped propagation exactly as DEC-004 predicted, and wrote 8 rows: 4 FAILED (one per Copy attempt) + 4 SUCCESS (bronzecopy_EUSupplyShares, bronze_EPI, bronze_WGI, bronze_procurement). Overall run reported Failed via fail_orchestrator_run. ALSO CONFIRMS the task's core premise: ensure_log_table_exists() printed 'Created table' — gold_pipeline_execution_log had never existed, so nothing had ever written it since task-011.

CRITERION 4 FAILED THEN FIXED 2026-07-27. The live 404 categorised as 'Unknown'. Root cause: PERMANENT_ERROR_PATTERNS carried '404 not found', but real Fabric text is 'status code 404 NotFound' (no space) in the HybridDeliveryException and 'The remote server returned an error: (404) Not Found.' in the inner System.Net.WebException — neither contains the literal '404 not found'. The whole pattern list had been written from imagination and never met live output; criterion 4 exists precisely to catch that. FIX: replaced guessed phrasings with HTTP-status semantics matching both real forms — 'status code NNN' and '(NNN)' — 4xx to PERMANENT (400/401/403/404/409 plus 'http request failed with client error'), 5xx + 429 to TRANSIENT (500/502/503/504/429/toomanyrequests). 429 correctness depends on categorize_error checking TRANSIENT first, since the permanent list also carries the generic 4xx marker; that ordering is now load-bearing and documented in-code. REGRESSION TEST: tests/test_error_categorization.py, 17 assertions, extracts categorize_error from the LIVE notebook via ast (same reference-implementation contract as test_key_generation.py) and anchors on the verbatim error string from run 742ff1ff. Suite now 111 passing.

test_protocol.summary: Prove the execution log receives both outcomes from a real orchestrated run.
